title: Dutch DPA fines Uber EUR 824 990 000 for unlawful automated decision-making and insufficient information on profiling
key_claim: The Dutch DPA fined Uber for fully automated deactivation of driver accounts and insufficient information on automated decision-making; the case began with complaints from 171 French drivers, covers 2018 to 2022, was led under the one-stop-shop procedure, and Uber has appealed.
frame_summary: Reports the Dutch authority's finding that Uber took fully automated decisions about drivers without adequate information, as a case handled under the one-stop-shop procedure.
verbatim_quote: Complaints from 171 French Uber drivers, submitted through the Ligue des droits de l’Homme (LDH)
verbatim_list: The case concerned incidents between 2018 and 2022.
Uber has appealed the fine, and there is no final judicial decision yet.

title: The Irish Data Protection Commission fines Google EUR 403 000 000 following Inquiry into Google's processing of location data
key_claim: The Irish DPC fined Google EUR 403 million over location-data processing between 25 May 2018 and 4 February 2020 and ordered compliance within 6 months.
frame_summary: Reports a second nine-figure GDPR fine in a month, this one on transparency and lawfulness of location data rather than automated decisions.

title: AP heeft Uber een boete van bijna 825 miljoen euro
key_claim: The Dutch DPA fined Uber nearly EUR 825 million on 21 August 2026; Uber's 2025 global turnover was about EUR 44.5 billion, the guideline cap is 4% of turnover (the fine is about 1.85% of that turnover, analyst calculation), an earlier 2024 fine was EUR 290 million, and the AP's vice-chair said a human should have looked first.
frame_summary: Reports the fine and its basis, setting it against Uber's turnover and earlier sanctions and quoting the regulator's view that a person should have reviewed the decisions.

title: Dutch regulator fines Uber 825 million euros over automated driver blocking
key_claim: The AP imposed a fine of 824,990,000 euros on Uber; the report links the case to the AP's draft consultation on meaningful human intervention and to the Commission's Digital Omnibus proposal, which would restructure Article 22.
frame_summary: Argues the Uber fine rests on the Article 22 ban that the Digital Omnibus proposes to recast, and ties it to the AP's draft guidance on genuine human review.

title: GDPR Procedural Regulation: A new era for cross-border enforcement?
key_claim: The GDPR Procedural Regulation applies in its entirety from 2 April 2027, sets a 15-month target for the lead authority's draft decision with a possible 12-month extension in exceptionally complex cases, and applies to investigations opened or lodged after that date.
frame_summary: Explains the new procedural clocks and rights that will govern cross-border GDPR cases from April 2027 without changing the GDPR's substantive rules.

title: EU Platform Work Directive: Uncertainty Ahead of the Implementation Deadline
key_claim: Member States have until 2 December 2026 to transpose the Platform Work Directive, which sets stricter requirements for automated monitoring and decision-making systems; transposition is at an early stage in many countries.
frame_summary: Argues that employers face uncertainty because many Member States have not settled how they will carry the Directive's algorithmic-management rules into national law.

title: Digital Omnibus: The Council Adopts Its Position, Simplifying the GDPR Without Dismantling It?
key_claim: Reports that the Council's Digital Omnibus mandate extends the breach-notification deadline from 72 to 96 hours, shifts cookie oversight to GDPR authorities, and may change in trilogues; the page does not describe any change by the Council to Article 22.
frame_summary: Argues the Council mandate trims GDPR procedure and cookie rules without removing the core data-protection principles.
